articles.title: iFood sofre ataque hacker que expõe dados de clientes, entregadores e representantes de restaurantes | G1
articles.standfirst: Clientes que tiveram dados expostos no ataque serão avisados pelo iFood por e-mail a partir desta quinta-feira (19). A empresa ainda não informou o número de afetados.
articles.summary: Clientes que tiveram dados expostos no ataque serão avisados pelo iFood por e-mail a partir desta quinta-feira (19). A empresa ainda não informou o número de afetados.
articles.body:
Entregador de aplicativo com bag do iFood. — Foto: Celso Tavares/G1

O iFood informou nesta quinta-feira (19) que criminosos invadiram seus sistemas e acessaram dados de clientes, representantes de restaurantes e entregadores.

Ao g1 , a empresa disse que ainda investiga o caso e, por isso, não pode confirmar quantas pessoas foram afetadas . A empresa começará a avisar os clientes atingidos por e-mail a partir desta quinta. (Saiba o que foi vazado) .

A invasão, segundo eles, ocorreu no sábado (14). O iFood não detalhou como os criminosos entraram em seus sistemas, mas afirmou que os serviços seguem funcionando normalmente.

Os invasores não tiveram acesso a senhas, cartões, meios de pagamento, saldos, extratos ou informações biométricas , disseram. "O iFood notificou a Agência Nacional de Proteção de Dados (ANPD) e colabora com a autoridade. A investigação e o monitoramento continuam", completou a companhia.

Quem foi afetado e quais dados foram expostos

Clientes e usuários do iFood Benefícios: apenas o número de telefone.

Representantes de restaurantes: o telefone cadastrado, o CPF ou ambos.

Entregadores: os dados expostos podem incluir nome, e-mail, telefone, endereço e CPF. Em alguns casos, também foram expostos os números da agência e da conta bancária .

O iFood orienta os clientes afetados a ficar atentos a ligações e e-mails com pedidos de senha, código de verificação ou pagamento. A empresa também recomenda desconfiar de links desconhecidos enviados em nome do iFood.

"O iFood não solicita senha, código de verificação ou dados de cartão por telefone, e-mail, SMS ou aplicativo de mensagem. Se puder, ative a verificação em duas etapas", afirmou a empresa.

Este é o segundo vazamento de dados pessoais envolvendo o iFood neste ano. Em junho, a empresa informou que cerca de 1,2 milhão de pessoas foram afetadas pelo primeiro vazamento .

Na ocasião, foram expostos dados como nome e CPF dos usuários. Segundo o iFood, as credenciais de acesso às contas (login e senha) não foram comprometidas.

articles.title: VÍDEO: lobo-marinho é visto descansando em praia no RJ | G1
articles.standfirst: Registro aconteceu na praia Cairuçu, nesta quinta-feira (19), em Paraty (RJ).
articles.summary: O lobo-marinho em Paraty foi identificado por biólogos na Praia Cairuçu; o animal costuma percorrer a costa brasileira entre o inverno e a primavera para repousar.
articles.body:
Um lobo-marinho-subantártico foi visto nesta quinta-feira (19), na praia Cairuçu das Pedras, em Paraty (RJ).

Imagens que circulam nas redes sociais estavam afirmando que o animal visto seria uma foca, mas, segundo o biólogo marinho Rafael Carvalho, se trata de um lobo-marinho-subantártico.

Ainda de acordo com o especialista, esses animais são das ilhas subantárticas e percorrem nossa costa entre o inverno e primavera.

VÍDEO: lobo-marinho é visto descansando em praia no RJ — Foto: Divulgação/Ronaldo dos Remédios

O biólogo informou ainda que o lobo-marinho-subantártico está bem, e que apenas parou no litoral para descansar.

Em casos de avistamento de animais, é importante respeitar o espaço do animal, caso ele procure a faixa de areia. Não tente alimenta-los, toca-los, não jogar água ou espantar para dentro do mar. O indicado é manter distância.

articles.title: Novo exame pode detectar doença cerebral ligada a pancadas na cabeça | G1
articles.standfirst: Encefalopatia traumática crônica hoje só pode ser confirmada após a morte; estudo encontrou um marcador associado a formas avançadas da doença em ex-jogadores de futebol americano.
articles.summary: Encefalopatia traumática crônica hoje só pode ser confirmada após a morte; estudo encontrou um marcador associado a formas avançadas da doença em ex-jogadores de futebol americano.
articles.body:
Esportes de contato, como o boxe, podem expor atletas a impactos repetidos na cabeça, fator associado à encefalopatia traumática crônica. — Foto: AP Photo/Etienne Laurent

Um exame de sangue pode ajudar, no futuro, a identificar em pessoas vivas uma doença cerebral associada a pancadas repetidas na cabeça , mostra um estudo récem-publicado nesta quinta-feira (19) na revista científica "JAMA".

A doença é a encefalopatia traumática crônica , conhecida pela sigla CTE em inglês.

Ela é associada à exposição repetida a impactos na cabeça e já foi identificada principalmente em atletas de esportes de contato , como futebol americano, boxe e rúgbi.

No Brasil, um dos casos mais conhecidos foi o de Éder Jofre , considerado o maior pugilista brasileiro de todos os tempos.

Ele morreu em 2022, aos 86 anos, e teve o cérebro doado para pesquisas na USP, que confirmaram encefalopatia traumática crônica após anos de sintomas como perda de memória e limitações motoras.

Hoje, o diagnóstico do quadro só pode ser confirmado após a morte, com a análise do cérebro do paciente.

Por causa disso, pesquisadores da Universidade de Boston e de outras instituições analisaram amostras de sangue de 21 ex-jogadores de futebol americano que participaram de pesquisas ainda em vida e depois doaram o cérebro para estudos.

Os cientistas procuraram no sangue uma substância chamada eMTBR-tau , relacionada ao acúmulo anormal da proteína tau no cérebro.

Os níveis desse marcador foram significativamente maiores nos ex-jogadores que depois tiveram formas avançadas da doença confirmadas na autópsia do que entre aqueles com estágios iniciais ou sem a doença.

Quanto maior a quantidade de tau encontrada no cérebro, maior também tendia a ser o nível do marcador no sangue.

O resultado abre caminho para um possível exame capaz de ajudar no diagnóstico ainda em vida. Esse teste, porém, ainda não existe para uso clínico.

Aliado a isso, o estudo ainda é bastante inicial: envolveu apenas os 21 homens e os resultados precisam ser confirmados em grupos maiores e mais diversos antes que o marcador possa ser usado para identificar a doença com segurança.

Há também outro obstáculo: a mesma substância pode aparecer em níveis elevados em pessoas com Alzheimer.

Cinco dos participantes com a doença ligada aos impactos na cabeça também apresentavam alterações cerebrais associadas ao Alzheimer.

Por isso, a tendência é que um futuro exame não dependa de apenas um marcador no sangue.

Os pesquisadores também analisaram uma segunda proteína mais ligada ao Alzheimer, que não apresentou associação com a doença causada pelos impactos repetidos.

Éder Jofre é considerado o maior pugilista brasileiro de todos os tempos. — Foto: Clayton de Souza/Estadão Conteúdo/Arquivo

A encefalopatia traumática crônica é uma doença neurodegenerativa progressiva associada à exposição repetida a impactos na cabeça, como os que podem ocorrer em esportes de contato.

A doença é marcada pelo acúmulo anormal da proteína tau em determinadas regiões do cérebro e é dividida em quatro estágios, dos mais leves aos mais avançados.

Os sintomas podem incluir perda de memória, alterações de humor e comportamento e dificuldades de raciocínio e julgamento, principalmente nas fases mais avançadas.

Como esses sinais também aparecem em outras doenças neurológicas, hoje a CTE só pode ser confirmada após a morte, por meio da análise do tecido cerebral .

A doença não tem cura conhecida, e uma das dificuldades para desenvolver tratamentos é justamente não haver uma forma validada de identificar com segurança quem tem CTE ainda em vida.

Encontrar uma forma confiável de detectá-la poderia não apenas melhorar o diagnóstico, mas também permitir que pesquisadores testem tratamentos e acompanhem se eles estão funcionando.

Por enquanto, porém, o novo marcador é uma pista promissora.

articles.title: PDV GM São José dos Campos: Inscrições abertas com bônus de R$ 133 mil | G1
articles.standfirst: Trabalhadores interessados devem preencher formulário online até às 17h de segunda-feira (23). Montadora tem limite de verba para o programa e vai priorizar funcionários com mais tempo de serviço.
articles.summary: O PDV da GM em São José dos Campos oferece sete salários e bônus de até R$ 133 mil para funcionários que se inscreverem no programa até a próxima segunda-feira.
articles.body:
Com bônus de até R$ 133 mil, GM abre inscrições para plano de demissão voluntária em São José dos Campos; veja prazo e critérios — Foto: Roosevelt Cassio

A General Motors (GM) abriu as inscrições para o Plano de Demissão Voluntária (PDV) destinado a funcionários da fábrica de São José dos Campos (SP). Os trabalhadores interessados em aderir ao programa devem preencher um formulário online até às 17h da próxima segunda-feira (23).

O link foi disponibilizado pela montadora ao meio-dia desta quarta-feira (18), segundo informações do Sindicato dos Metalúrgicos. A inscrição, no entanto, não garante a participação no programa, pois a empresa estabeleceu um limite de verba para as adesões.

De acordo com o comunicado enviado pela GM aos funcionários, a montadora estabeleceu como meta a adesão de 108 funcionários ao PDV. Caso o número de interessados ultrapasse esse limite, a seleção será feita de acordo com o tempo de serviço na empresa e, em caso de empate, pela ordem de inscrição.

Já se o número de adesões ficar abaixo da meta, a montadora afirma que poderá buscar “outras alternativas para seguir com as reduções indispensáveis” no quadro de funcionários.

A partir desta terça-feira (24), o setor de Recursos Humanos (RH) começará a entrar em contato com os funcionários interessados no PDV, para informar se o trabalhador vai participar do plano e os próximos passos. A saída dos trabalhadores ocorrerá somente após a convocação e a assinatura dos documentos.

O programa é destinado aos funcionários horistas da área de Manufatura da fábrica de São José dos Campos que foram contratados antes de 1º de março de 2019 e que estejam com o contrato de trabalho ativo.

O plano foi aprovado pelos trabalhadores em assembleias realizadas na terça-feira (17) , com a participação de cerca de 3 mil funcionários do primeiro e do segundo turno.

Para incentivar a adesão ao PDV, a empresa está oferecendo salários, bônus em dinheiro, carro, entre outros benefícios, veja:

Convênio médico gratuito por 24 meses ou R$ 48 mil em dinheiro;

Um Chevrolet Onix zero-quilômetro ou R$ 85 mil em dinheiro.

Carro zero, bônus de até R$ 133 mil e sete salários: veja o que a GM oferece em PDV em São José dos Campos — Foto: Foto 1: Divulgação/Sindicato dos Metalúrgicos | Foto 2: Divulgação/Chevrolet

Os valores em dinheiro podem chegar a R$ 133 mil, caso o trabalhador escolha receber os R$ 48 mil no lugar do convênio médico e os R$ 85 mil no lugar do carro. Esse valor é pago além dos sete salários nominais.

O comunicado da GM também informa que o veículo poderá ser escolhido entre um Onix Turbo automático ou um Onix Plus Turbo automático. A montadora terá até 180 dias após o pagamento das verbas rescisórias para entregar o carro. Despesas como documentação, IPVA e seguro ficam por conta do funcionário.

Segundo a montadora, o programa faz parte de um processo de adequação das operações às demandas do mercado e à sustentabilidade do negócio. Em assembleia, a empresa também justificou a proposta com a redução do volume de produção e a necessidade de ajustar o quadro de funcionários.

O último PDV aberto pela GM em São José dos Campos havia sido em junho de 2025, quando 359 trabalhadores aderiram ao plano.

A unidade produz os modelos S10 e Trailblazer e tem cerca de 3,2 mil funcionários.

O g1 procurou a General Motors, mas não recebeu retorno até a última atualização desta reportagem.

articles.title: Morre aos 104 anos militar cearense que lutou na 2ª Guerra Mundial | G1
articles.standfirst: Mais de 300 cearenses lutaram na Segunda Guerra Mundial nas Forças Expedicionárias Brasileiras, e o tenente Geraldo Rodrigues era o último vivo.
articles.summary: Mais de 300 cearenses lutaram na Segunda Guerra Mundial nas Forças Expedicionárias Brasileiras, e o tenente Geraldo Rodrigues era o último vivo.
articles.body:
Morreu nesta quinta-feira (19), aos 104 anos, o tenente Geraldo Rodrigues de Oliveira, ex-combatente da Força Expedicionária Brasileira (FEB) e o último cearense que estava vivo a lutar na Segunda Guerra Mundial. A morte foi confirmada pela 10ª Região Militar do Exército, responsável pelos estados do Ceará e Piauí.

Natural de Assaré, no interior do Ceará, tenente Geraldo nasceu em 22 de fevereiro de 1922. Conforme o Exército, ele decidiu se alistar nas Forças Armadas enquanto ouvia a programação de rádio, que trazia notícias da guerra no mundo e fazia apelos para jovens brasileiros defenderem o país.

O cearense serviu no 23º e no 29º Batalhão de Caçadores e embarcou no navio General Meigs rumo à Itália, onde participou da Segunda Guerra Mundial. Ele ficou no país por cerca de oito meses, quando participou da Batalha de Monte Castelo, uma das mais famosas batalhas nas quais os soldados brasileiros lutaram.

Morre aos 104 anos tenente Geraldo Rodrigues, último cearense que lutou na Segunda Guerra Mundial — Foto: Divulgação/10ª Região Militar

Geraldo era o último cearense vivo a ter participado da Segunda Guerra Mundial. Até o início de 2026, eram dois pracinhas ainda vivos no Ceará: Geraldo e o sargento José Barbosa Sobrinho . Sobrinho, porém, morreu em abril deste ano.

Após voltar da Itália, o tenente Geraldo se estabeleceu onde Fortaleza, onde casou e teve cinco filhos. Em fevereiro deste ano, a 10ª Região Militar celebrou o aniversário de 104 anos de Geraldo em uma festa com familiares e militares . O tenente viveu na capital cearense até sua morte, nesta quinta-feira.

"Seu exemplo de coragem, patriotismo e dedicação à Pátria permanecerá vivo na memória de nossa instituição e na história de nossa Nação. Nossos sinceros sentimentos aos familiares, amigos e a todo o povo cearense neste momento de despedida e merecida reverência", disse a 10ª Região Militar em nota de pesar.

O Brasil enviou mais de 25 mil homens para lutar na Segunda Guerra Mundial, dos quais mais de 15 mil eram combatentes e os demais exerciam outras funções militares.

Dos brasileiros enviados para o conflito, cerca de 377 eram cearenses, entre eles o tenente Geraldo e o sargento José Sobrinho. Dos 377 cearenses, seis morreram na Europa - cinco em batalha e um em acidente de carro.

articles.title: 8 days, 4 countries and no checked-in luggage: Etihad Airways directed to compensate Kanyakumari passenger left without clothes, toiletries, cash and medicines during international pilgrimage across Jordan, Israel, Palestine and Egypt
articles.summary: THIRUVANANTHAPURAM: The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Thiruvananthapuram, has directed UAE-based Etihad Airways to pay Rs 25,000 as
articles.body: THIRUVANANTHAPURAM: The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Thiruvananthapuram, has directed UAE-based Etihad Airways to pay Rs 25,000 as compensation and Rs 5,000 towards litigation costs to a passenger whose checked-in baggage was not delivered during an eight-day international pilgrimage tour.The order, issued on November 12, 2026, came on a complaint filed by Alfred Varghese of Kanyakumari. Varghese was travelling with a group from Thiruvananthapuram to Abu Dhabi, Jordan, Israel, Palestine and Egypt between December 20 and 28, 2015.His baggage was short-landed at Queen Alia Airport in Amman, Jordan, leaving him without clothes, toiletries, cash and medicines that he claimed were required for his heart condition.The commission held that the airline was responsible for ensuring the safe and timely delivery of checked-in baggage and found that the delay amounted to deficiency in service. It noted that the baggage was recovered the next day but could not be delivered during the tour as the passenger had moved between destinations. The airline had apologised and offered US$40 as compensation.However, the commission also observed that passengers are advised not to place cash and essential medicines in checked-in baggage. It further noted that Varghese had not produced bills for emergency purchases and rejected his allegation of unfair trade practice.The commission partly allowed his complaint and ordered Etihad Airways to make the payment within 30 days of receiving the order. Failure to pay the compensation within the stipulated period would attract interest at 9% per annum from the date of the order until realisation, the order said.Stay updated with the latest Thiruvananthapuram news. articles.title: Somali-American Abdi Daisane is Minnesota's new lawmaker. DHS says his wife entered US illegally in 2023; 'I smuggled myself and jumped over the wall for my love'
articles.summary: The wife of an incoming Minnesota Democratic lawmaker has been living in the United States illegally after crossing the US-Mexico border on foot in 2023,
articles.body: The wife of an incoming Minnesota Democratic lawmaker has been living in the United States illegally after crossing the US-Mexico border on foot in 2023, the Department of Homeland Security has confirmed, adding a new immigration controversy to the politician's growing list of troubles. Ayan Ahmed Aidid, 30, the wife of Abdi Daisane, a Democrat who won Minnesota House District 14A on November 3, was apprehended by Border Patrol agents after entering the country, but was subsequently released under the Biden administration, DHS told Alpha News.“Ayan Ahmed Aidid is a 30-year-old illegal alien from Somalia who illegally entered the United States on foot through the southern border on April 2, 2023,” a DHS spokesperson said.“She was arrested by [US Customs and Border Protection] four miles west of the San Ysidro Port of Entry but then RELEASED into the country by the Biden administration, completely unvetted, despite having no legal permission to be in the United States,” the spokesperson added.Immigration and Customs Enforcement also publicly identified Aidid on Wednesday, reiterating that US immigration laws apply to everyone, regardless of their political connections.But this was hardly a secret as Aidid had previously spoken publicly about her border crossing. In a November 2023 interview with BBC News Somali, she described climbing over the US-Mexico border fence to reunite with Daisane. “I smuggled myself and jumped over the wall for my love,” she said, according to an English translation of the interview cited by Alpha News.Aidid, who also writes poetry under the name Ayaan Kaaba, reportedly crossed the border in April 2023.Daycare receives 12 more violationsThe immigration revelations came alongside fresh scrutiny of Daisane's childcare business, Blooming Kids Child Care Center in St Cloud, Minnesota. The daycare received another 12 licensing violations during a state review on October 8, less than four weeks before Daisane defeated Republican Mike Conway in the election. The violations included hazardous objects within children's reach, unsanitary conditions, improperly maintained fire extinguishers, missing immunisation and allergy records, inadequate staff supervision and training, and deficiencies in required childcare programme plans.Daisane's daycare has received more than $7.29 million through Minnesota's Child Care Assistance Program since 2018, according to records. It also received nearly $600,000 in approved claims through a federally funded food programme.Some of the food-programme claims were approved under the sponsorship of Partners in Nutrition, a nonprofit that recently agreed to an $18.5 million settlement over allegations of widespread fraud. Blooming Kids was not named in that case.The Minnesota Attorney General's Office has previously said the daycare is not among the facilities being investigated in connection with the Partners in Nutrition case. Daisane has dismissed allegations linking his business to Minnesota's fraud scandals as baseless.Daisane's political backgroundDaisane made history earlier this month by becoming the first Somali-born lawmaker elected to represent central Minnesota. He defeated Conway with 51.6% of the vote, flipping a seat Republicans had held for decades.He became a US citizen in 2014. The incoming lawmaker will now represent St Cloud and surrounding communities in the Minnesota Legislature.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.summary: US President Donald Trump appeared to doze off during Chinese President Xi Jinping's speech at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) plenary
articles.body: US President Donald Trump appeared to doze off during Chinese President Xi Jinping's speech at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) plenary session on Thursday, with his eyes seen closed as the Chinese leader addressed the gathering in Shenzhen.The moment came two days into Trump's Asia tour, which began with the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit in the Philippines before he arrived in Shenzhen, China, on Wednesday.Trump's visit has also drawn attention to his personal diplomacy with major world leaders, particularly Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin.The three leaders held their first-ever trilateral meeting in Shenzhen on Thursday, agreeing to pursue reforms at the United Nations, increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products and hold discussions on reducing nuclear risks.Trump, Xi and Putin agree on UN reforms, energy cooperationAccording to a joint declaration released by Chinese and Russian officials, the three countries committed to advancing reforms at the United Nations to "more effectively address global challenges".They also agreed to increase the production and supply of petroleum products to ensure stable energy flows and engage in dialogue to reduce nuclear risks and prevent the proliferation of nuclear weapons.The declaration also addressed the International Criminal Court (ICC), stating that state officials should enjoy immunity from its prosecutions and warning that the court must not abuse its jurisdiction. Russian President Putin is wanted by the ICC.Xi described the meeting as positive, constructive and “fruitful”, while Putin said the discussions were “open and candid”.The declaration, however, made no mention of the wars in Ukraine or Iran, two issues Trump said he had raised with the leaders earlier in the day.Personal diplomacy takes centre stageThe warmth displayed by Trump, Xi and Putin during their interactions also drew attention, with the leaders exchanging friendly greetings. Xi hugged Trump when the US president arrived on Wednesday evening.In his public remarks, Xi highlighted the importance of personal ties between the two leaders, saying their role in guiding US-China relations “has no substitute”.The summit also highlighted Trump's enthusiasm for a “G2” arrangement between Washington and Beijing, Ali Wyne, senior research and advocacy adviser at the International Crisis Group, said in emailed comments.“U.S. allies and partners understandably worry about where that sentiment leaves them in Washington’s strategic outlook, regardless of the assurances that they may receive from top Trump advisors and members of Congress,” he added.Trump holds separate meeting with PutinTrump also held a separate bilateral meeting with Putin on the sidelines of the APEC Summit. It was the first time the two leaders had held talks since their discussions in Alaska last year failed to broker a deal to ease Russia's war in Ukraine.After joining Putin for the meeting, Trump described the Russian president as “my friend” and said, “Wonderful things can come out of this — or at least start.”The two leaders shook hands before their talks, with Trump adding, “We’ve had a great relationship for many years.”The meeting lasted roughly 40 minutes.You use AI every day. articles.title: Trump calls Vance-negotiated Iran deal a 'waste of time' but says signing it wasn't a mistake
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump discusses the controversial Iran memorandum of understanding, calling it a 'waste of time', while defending the decision to sign, and highlighting ongoing diplomatic tensions.
articles.body: US President Donald Trump has described the memorandum of understanding negotiated by Vice President JD Vance with Iran in June as a “waste of time”, but said signing the agreement was not a mistake.Speaking to Fox News reporter Jacqui Heinrich during his visit to China on Wednesday, Trump said he had not wanted to pursue the arrangement but had listened to members of his administration.“I didn’t like doing it, but I listened to people,” he said.The agreement collapsed in July after Iran attacked several commercial vessels amid a dispute over postwar control of the Strait of Hormuz. Trump said the negotiations had given Washington a clearer understanding of Tehran, adding that he had concluded Iran could not be trusted.Trump also rejected suggestions that Vance had been removed from Iran negotiations because of the failed agreement. However, he acknowledged a difference of opinion with the vice president over whether the US should have gone to war with Iran.Referring to Vance's position on the conflict, Trump said the vice president had left out one point when discussing whether the war should have been pursued.“If we had it to do again, would you do [the war] again? And the answer is absolutely yes,” Trump said.He added that the administration's decision would be judged favourably in the long term and that concerns over the upcoming elections would not guide his actions.Last week, Trump said he wanted Vance to devote his attention to addressing benefit fraud in Democrat-led cities and states rather than handling international negotiations. However, sources told the New York Post that the vice president remained involved in the Iran portfolio and could resume his negotiating role if there was progress in talks.An administration official told the newspaper that Trump was signalling strategic patience and could send Vance back to negotiations if a suitable agreement emerged.US special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are currently leading Washington's negotiations with Tehran.Earlier this month, Trump said the war with Iran was effectively over but indicated that the US naval blockade of Iranian ports would remain in place.You use AI every day. articles.title: From capture of Maduro to inking military deal: Venezuela's stunning U-turn with the US
articles.summary: The US went from storming Venezuela to capture its president to shaking hands with his successor over a military deal.
articles.body: The US went from storming Venezuela to capture its president to shaking hands with his successor over a military deal.Less than a year after American forces toppled Nicolás Maduro's government and seized him in a daring raid, Washington is now rebuilding defence ties with Caracas in one of the most striking turnarounds in recent US foreign policy.The agreement was signed on Wednesday during US defence secretary Pete Hegseth's meeting with Venezuela's interim President Delcy Rodríguez at the presidential palace in Caracas.The deal marks the restoration of military cooperation between the two countries, which was severed in 2005 under former Venezuelan president Hugo Chávez.Although the full details of the agreement have not been made public, Rodríguez said it would focus on training Venezuela's armed forces, upgrading their operational equipment and providing access to new technology to tackle shared security threats.Hegseth described the agreement as a major shift in bilateral relations, saying Venezuela had gone from being Washington's "most aggressive regional threat" to a "compliant security partner" in less than 12 months.Addressing security threats in the region, he said the partnership would operate through the US-led Americas Counter Cartel Coalition and warned drug-trafficking networks and armed groups using Venezuela as a safe haven that Washington would hunt them down.Rodríguez, meanwhile, called the agreement "extraordinarily relevant" to bilateral relations, saying both countries had turned a period of difficult relations into one of cooperation and mutual benefit. She said the arrangement would help Venezuela strengthen its armed forces and improve their ability to confront common threats.The agreement comes less than a year after Washington launched a military operation to capture Maduro, marking one of the most dramatic interventions in Latin America in recent years.On January 3, US forces carried out strikes in Venezuela, including in the capital Caracas, as American troops moved to seize Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores. The operation ended with both being taken into US custody and flown to New York to face drug-trafficking and conspiracy charges, which they have denied.The operation followed months of escalating pressure from the Trump administration, which had accused Maduro of running a narco-terrorism network and facilitating drug trafficking into the United States.Washington had increased its reward for information leading to his capture to $50 million late last year. Maduro, meanwhile, had publicly challenged the US to come and get him, a remark Hegseth recalled during his visit to Caracas. "Well, we answered that call," the US defence secretary said on Wednesday.Maduro's capture brought an abrupt end to his presidency, with his former vice-president Delcy Rodríguez taking over as interim president.The same administration that Washington had confronted militarily is now engaging with the US on defence cooperation, military training and regional security.The latest agreement, therefore, marks a striking reversal in bilateral relations, with the US moving from forcibly removing Venezuela's leader to building a military partnership with his successor in less than a year.You use AI every day. articles.title: Musk's SpaceXSI denies liability over Grok-generated sexualised images of UK lawmaker
articles.summary: Elon Musk's SpaceX Super Intelligence (SpaceXSI) has denied legal responsibility for fake sexualised images of a British lawmaker generated using its Grok
articles.body: Elon Musk's SpaceX Super Intelligence (SpaceXSI) has denied legal responsibility for fake sexualised images of a British lawmaker generated using its Grok AI platform. In a written defence filed at London's High Court on October 29, the company argued that AI-generated images that are obviously fictitious cannot violate a person's right to privacy. The response came in a lawsuit filed by Jess Asato, a member of Britain's governing Labour Party, who is seeking an order to prevent Grok from creating manipulated images of her.SpaceXSI has denied allegations of misuse of private information and breaches of data protection laws. It has also contested Asato's request for an order requiring it to "implement effective and permanent technical measures" to stop Grok from generating manipulated images of her.'Fictitious and implausible'In its defence, lawyers for SpaceX Super Intelligence LLC said the company had removed AI-generated images of Asato that violated its terms. These included a video showing her "being chloroformed and prepared for a sexual assault".However, the company argued that other images it had allowed to remain online were clearly artificial.They said such content "would be understood by reasonable and sensible persons viewing that content to be AI-generated, fictitious and implausible ... rather than as realistic images".On this basis, the company argued that Asato could not claim a reasonable expectation of privacy.SpaceXSI also denied violating her data protection rights. It argued that it "did not determine the content of the relevant users' prompts".Lawmaker challenges company's defenceAsato hit back at the company's position on Thursday, saying that developers of powerful AI tools must be held accountable for their products."SpaceX SI wants to have it both ways," she said."The company admits it built the AI model, rewrote user requests to add its own graphic details, pulled images from across the internet, and published the results from an account it controls," she said, adding: "Yet it also claims it is a neutral bystander without legal responsibility".Asato has accused the company of designing and training Grok in a way that enabled users to generate sexualised images of her. Her lawsuit alleges misuse of private information and breaches of data protection laws.A test case for AI companiesThe lawsuit is among the first cases to examine whether an AI developer can be held legally responsible for the way its system is designed and the content it generates.The court's eventual findings could have implications for similar cases involving AI-generated content and the responsibilities of companies developing such tools.Grok faces scrutiny across countriesGrok, which is available through Musk's social media platform X, has faced regulatory scrutiny in several countries following an outcry over its use to generate sexualised images of people without their consent.In mid-January, xAI said it had restricted image editing on Grok. It also said it had blocked users from generating images of people in revealing clothing "where it's illegal".However, a Reuters investigation in early February found that Grok continued to generate sexualised images even after the restrictions were introduced. The platform did so even when users explicitly warned that the people depicted had not consented.In July, xAI sued a man in the US, alleging that he had misused Grok to create child sexual abuse material. The case was among the first of its kind brought by an AI company.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Prince Harry says he is ready to rejoin British Army if needed amid Russia-Ukraine war; Duke of Sussex served 10 years, completed two Afghanistan tours as Apache helicopter pilot
articles.summary: Prince Harry has indicated that he would put on his military uniform again if the situation demanded it.
articles.body: Prince Harry has indicated that he would put on his military uniform again if the situation demanded it. The Duke of Sussex made the revelation during an interview with The Telegraph while visiting Ukraine, where he met wounded soldiers, veterans and athletes preparing for the 2027 Invictus Games.Asked about the possibility of returning to the armed forces, Harry said he would be ready to serve alongside former and serving military personnel if called upon."If asked to sign up again, if the need is there, then I will 100% be there to serve my country alongside my fellow veterans and service personnel," he told the publication.The 42-year-old royal also expressed concern over the current geopolitical situation, warning that people should not underestimate the threat posed by the Russia-Ukraine conflict."I think we should all be nervous, absolutely," he said, adding that Britain needed to be prepared and that former service personnel should be ready to serve again.Prince Harry says Europe has 'woken up to the threat' from RussiaDuring his conversation with The Telegraph in the western Ukrainian city of Lviv, Harry said Europe had finally recognised the seriousness of the Russian threat. He argued that the danger had been present for years and that the absence of direct military attacks did not mean other countries were unaffected by the conflict."Just because there's not drones, bullets, and rockets flying at us doesn't mean that we're not at war," he said. "I feel like we've been at war for the last decade."The Duke also expressed concern that European countries could become divided among themselves instead of maintaining a united response to Russian aggression.Harry's remarks come amid growing concerns among European defence and intelligence officials about Russian activities, including cyberattacks, sabotage and other forms of hybrid warfare. His comments reflected his view that countries need to take the wider security threat seriously rather than focus only on conventional military attacks.Harry comments on Donald Trump's approach to UkraineThe Duke of Sussex also spoke about the difference between public sentiment in the United States and the approach taken by the administration of President Donald Trump towards Ukraine.Without directly naming Trump, Harry suggested that American public opinion was more supportive of Ukraine than the position adopted by the current administration."I think there's been a big separation between what American society feels regarding support for Ukraine, which I think is incredibly high and always has been, compared to a certain group – or in this case an administration that was perhaps thinking about it differently," he said.Harry also called for greater international support for Ukraine, expressing confidence in Europe's collective response while suggesting that stronger American backing would be welcome.Prince Harry's military career and Afghanistan toursHarry served in the British Army for a decade, from 2005 to 2015, after completing officer cadet training at the Royal Military Academy Sandhurst. During his military career, he undertook two tours of Afghanistan and served as an Apache helicopter pilot, eventually reaching the rank of Captain.After leaving the armed forces, he remained involved in supporting military personnel and veterans. In 2014, he founded the Invictus Games, an international sporting competition for wounded, injured and sick service personnel and veterans.The competition uses sport as a platform to support rehabilitation and help former service members rebuild their confidence and sense of purpose.Prince Harry visits Ukraine for Invictus Games preparationsHarry's latest trip marked his fourth visit to Ukraine since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in 2022 and his second visit to the country this year.During the unannounced visit, he met Ukrainian soldiers and veterans and visited the Superhumans Centre in Lviv, a specialised medical, prosthetics and rehabilitation facility supporting people injured in the war.His visit also coincided with trials to select athletes who will represent Ukraine at the 2027 Invictus Games, scheduled to take place in Birmingham, England.While interacting with injured military personnel, Harry expressed admiration for Ukraine's resilience and said there was much the international community could learn from the country's experience.He also told injured Ukrainian soldiers that he hoped to bring the Invictus Games to their country once they had won the war.Harry says Invictus Games changed perceptions of wounded veteransDuring the interview, the Duke also reflected on how the Invictus Games had changed public attitudes towards veterans living with life-changing injuries.Recalling the early days of the initiative, Harry said that people in the UK were initially uncomfortable around veterans with visible disabilities."When we started Invictus, over 10 years ago, people — parents, mums and dads in the United Kingdom — would take their children over to the other side of the road, away from the veteran who had one leg and was limping," he said.He recalled how injured veterans were once viewed with concern, sympathy and pity, with some people associating their military experiences with negative stereotypes.Harry believes the Games helped change that perception by allowing people to recognise veterans for their abilities, achievements and contributions to society."Ten years later, those parents in countries like England are taking their children across the road to go and meet the veteran, to go and speak to the guy who has one leg, and to hear his story," he said.He added that the shift in public perception had helped strengthen national resilience and recognition of military personnel.You use AI every day. articles.title: Indian national Anuj Kumar accused of molesting 14-year-old boy while driving Uber in California was in US illegally, DHS says he was released from jail despite ICE detainer
articles.summary: An Indian national accused of sexually assaulting a 14-year-old boy while working as an Uber driver in California is in the United States illegally and
articles.body: An Indian national accused of sexually assaulting a 14-year-old boy while working as an Uber driver in California is in the United States illegally and was released from jail despite an immigration detention request from federal authorities, according to the Department of Homeland Security.Anuj Kumar Kumar, 32, allegedly molested the teenager during an Uber ride to a school-related concert at San Jose State University in September. He was arrested on September 13 and charged with felony lewd and lascivious acts involving a minor.But Kumar was released from the Santa Clara County Main Jail on Sunday after posting bail, despite ICE having lodged a detainer against him, The Daily Wire reported. This happened as the sheriff's office did not notify ICE before releasing Kumar, nearly two months after his arrest, the DHS alleged.ICE vs Sheriff's OfficeThe Santa Clara County Sheriff's Office defended the release, saying it does not hold individuals in custody solely on the basis of immigration detainers because of California law. The development prompted a sharp response from DHS, which accused California's sanctuary policies of allowing an alleged child predator to walk free. “Now, instead of a controlled transfer between two law enforcement agencies, ICE has to conduct a dangerous operation to arrest and remove this illegal alien child predator before he reoffends,” a DHS spokesperson told The Daily Wire.The spokesperson added that restrictions on cooperation between local law enforcement and federal immigration authorities force ICE officers to conduct more visible operations to locate individuals released from local jails.What happened during the Uber ride?According to the Santa Clara County District Attorney's Office, Kumar picked up the 14-year-old boy from his parents' home in Sunnyvale on September 12. The teenager was travelling to a concert at San Jose State University as part of a school project.Kumar allegedly dropped him off at the wrong location on campus, forcing the boy to get back into the vehicle for a ride to the correct destination. During the second leg of the journey, Kumar allegedly asked the teenager to kiss him and perform oral sex on him multiple times, prosecutors said. He also allegedly touched the boy repeatedly and pulled his head towards his groin while making the requests.The teenager tried to get out of the vehicle but could not open the door from inside, believing that the child safety lock had been activated. He eventually managed to escape and immediately told his friends about the alleged assault. He also sent a text message to his parents.San Jose police arrested Kumar the following day.The Santa Clara County District Attorney's Office subsequently obtained a grand jury indictment against him.DHS says Indian national illegally crossed US border in 2023DHS said Kumar entered the United States illegally in January 2023 after crossing the southern border with a group of 16 other foreign nationals. According to the department, border authorities released him into the country without proper vetting.ICE lodged an immigration detainer against Kumar on September 14, one day after his arrest, but the local sheriff's office did not hold him when he posted bail. The sheriff's office said its decision was consistent with California law, which generally limits local authorities' ability to detain people solely on the basis of federal immigration requests.District attorney criticizes UberSanta Clara County District Attorney Jeff Rosen also criticized Uber over the alleged assault, arguing that the company had failed to introduce adequate safeguards to protect passengers. “This is not just the story of the sexual assault of a child; it is the story of a company that refuses to put up appropriate safeguards to prevent these criminal tragedies from happening,” Rosen said. He also expressed frustration over what he described as the company's unwillingness to inform law enforcement about sexual assault allegations involving its drivers.Uber said it had permanently banned Kumar from its platform and was assisting law enforcement with the investigation.“What's been reported is horrifying, and our hearts go out to the survivor and their family. Sexual assault is a devastating crime that has no place on our platform,” the company said. Uber also pointed to its driver background checks and safety features, including an emergency button, audio-recording options and tools allowing riders to share their trips.You use AI every day. articles.body: “Looksmaxxing” influencer Clavicular, whose real name is Braden Peters, has been indicted on two counts of rape and one count of providing alcohol to a minor in Massachusetts. The 20-year-old is accused of sexually assaulting a 17-year-old girl at his family’s home in Cape Cod in May 2025. Peters has denied the allegations through his lawyer and previously pleaded not guilty in court.Clavicular faces two rape charges over alleged 2025 incident involving 17-year-old girlAccording to WCVB, Peters was indicted on November 13, following an investigation into the allegations. The case is now moving forward in Barnstable Superior Court, where he faces two felony rape counts and one misdemeanor charge related to providing alcohol to someone underage.The allegations date back to May 23, 2025, when the girl reportedly visited Peters at his family’s home in Chatham, Cape Cod. According to the police account reported by WCVB, the girl told investigators that she had met Peters through Instagram and had travelled to his home after he arranged an Uber ride for her.She also alleged that Peters gave her alcohol while he was livestreaming on Twitch. Police reviewed parts of the broadcast and reported hearing the teenager say, “Wait, I’m so drunk though.”The girl later told police that she had fallen asleep at the house and woke up to Peters sexually assaulting her. She said she had not agreed to the sexual encounter.The case first moved through Orleans District Court, where Peters appeared on October 22. He pleaded not guilty and was released after posting $10,000 bail. The judge also ordered him to surrender his passport, stay away from the alleged victim and not post about the case online.According to WCVB’s November 18 report, no hearings had been scheduled in the Superior Court case at that time.Braden Peters denies rape allegations as Clavicular’s criminal case moves forwardPeters has strongly rejected the accusations. His lawyer told Fox News that he denied all charges and allegations against him. His legal team has also argued that the sexual encounter was consensual. Peters has not been convicted, and the allegations remain before the court.The case also involves a civil lawsuit filed by the alleged victim in Florida in April 2026. The woman, who uses the name Alorah Ziva on social media, accused Peters of sexually assaulting her when she was 17. He wrote, “Trying to get my attention in anyway possible, a lawsuit? Seriously… really petty of you.”In another post, he added, “Happens to all successful young men, people try to come for your money. His content often discusses facial features, fitness and other ways people try to change their looks.This is not his first legal issue. articles.body: Lucknow: After eight years of suspension, senior IPS officer Jasvir Singh has been reinstated in service, but with a departmental penalty of demotion to the Additional Director General (ADG) rank, costing him a possible promotion to Director General (DG). The 1992-batch officer has been reinstated following the approval of the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC), with the demotion order remaining in force until a day before his retirement on Jan 31, 2028.State govt issued his reinstatement order on Nov 17, 2026, attaching him to the ADG, Police Headquarters, although he has not been assigned any regular responsibility so far. Govt viewed his remarks as a violation of the All India Services (Conduct) Rules and sought an explanation from him.While the process of seeking his clarification was underway, Singh went on leave. According to the govt order, he was suspended for remaining absent from duty since Feb 4, 2019, without prior information or permission from the competent authority.Singh has previously been associated with several high-profile investigations. articles.title: Will reverse Greg Abbott's H-1B hiring freeze: Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa says schools need foreign teachers
articles.summary: Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa has said she will reverse outgoing Governor Greg Abbott's order freezing the hiring of H-1B visa holders at state
articles.body: Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa has said she will reverse outgoing Governor Greg Abbott's order freezing the hiring of H-1B visa holders at state agencies and public universities, arguing that the state cannot afford to lose access to foreign workers, particularly teachers, even as she acknowledged widespread abuses of the visa programme. In an interview with The Texas Tribune published November 18, Hinojosa said Abbott's restrictions did not make sense and accused his administration of turning the H-1B issue into a political and cultural battle.“Yeah, that does not make sense to me. I will tell you, I'm not doing culture wars. That's not what I was elected to do,” Hinojosa said when asked whether she would rescind the executive order.The Democratic governor-elect, who defeated Republican Greg Abbott in the November 3 election, said she intended to review and reverse several of his executive orders when she takes office on January 19, 2027. The H-1B hiring freeze is among the measures she specifically identified for reversal. She explained that her opposition was not to a scrutiny of the programme itself, but to a blanket restriction that could hurt institutions struggling to recruit qualified employees.“There are abuses when it comes to H-1Bs, absolutely,” she said, arguing that companies should not receive taxpayer-funded incentives for creating jobs only to use that money to hire H-1B workers. “Companies should not be getting a bunch of tax breaks for jobs only to then use that money to hire H-1B employees. That's wrong. That's happening right now. I don't support that,” she said.Hinojosa also cited her experience as a labour lawyer, saying she had encountered serious exploitation of foreign workers employed through the H-1B programme.“And I'm a labor lawyer. As a labor lawyer, I have worked in law firms that have dealt with and seen terrible abuses of H-1B workers,” she said.She said abuses of the program should not become a reason to impose sweeping restrictions on employers. “We need to make sure that we are smart about how we are approaching this. It's not a one-size-fits-all,” she said.H-1B teachers: Texas schools depend on foreign workersOne of Hinojosa's strongest arguments against Abbott's order was the dependence of several Texas school districts on foreign teachers.She said many districts have increasingly turned to H-1B visa holders because they are unable to recruit enough American teachers willing to work in their schools.“A lot of school districts hire H-1B teachers because we can't get teachers here in this state who want to work for school districts anymore,” she said.Rather than abruptly restricting access to foreign teachers, Hinojosa said the state should work with school districts to build a stronger domestic teaching workforce.“What we have to do is be a partner, so that we alleviate and minimize the need for H-1B teachers, but that we are working with our school districts so that we have a highly qualified pool of teachers here within our own state for our schools,” she added.What Abbott's H-1B order meantAbbott announced the restrictions on January 27, 2026, directing Texas state agencies and public institutions of higher education to stop filing new H-1B visa petitions without written permission from the Texas Workforce Commission.The restriction is scheduled to remain in effect until May 31, 2027, the end of the Texas Legislature's next regular session.Under the directive, agencies and universities were also required to submit detailed information about their H-1B workforce, including the number of sponsored workers, their countries of origin, job classifications and visa expiration dates. They were also asked to demonstrate that qualified Texans had been given a reasonable opportunity to apply for positions filled by foreign workers.Abbott justified the move by arguing that taxpayer-funded employment opportunities should go to Texans first.“State government must lead by example and ensure that employment opportunities — particularly those funded with taxpayer dollars — are filled by Texans first,” he said when announcing the directive.The restrictions affect new sponsorship petitions rather than automatically terminating the status or employment of existing H-1B workers. However, they could complicate future hiring and visa renewals for public institutions.Hinojosa's proposed reversal would mark a significant policy shift for Texas, particularly for its public universities, research institutions and school districts that rely on international talent. articles.body: SRINAGAR: Three leopards, including two female cubs aged 8-9 months, were found dead in the forests of north Kashmir’s Kunzar area, prompting J&K’s wildlife protection department to file an FIR Thursday against unknown people after autopsies raised suspicion of poisoning.Wildlife official Shahid Sultan said the cubs were found dead on Nov 17, with no visible injury marks. Their bodies were kept overnight at the department’s control room in Tangmarg because a veterinarian was unavailable. Autopsies were conducted the next day. On Wednesday, police informed the department about another dead leopard, an 8-9-year-old male. All three were found in the same area, though not together, Sultan said.“The doctors in their reports have mentioned a suspected case of poisoning,” he said, adding they had also raised the possibility of infectious poisoning, suspecting the animals might have eaten contaminated meat, possibly a rabid dog. Samples were collected for forensic examination to establish the cause of death. “We have not come across such a case of suspected poisoning before,” he said.Leopard sightings are common, particularly in north Kashmir, where mountainous terrain and expanding apple orchards provide suitable habitat. articles.title: Hunter Biden slams Trump for ‘great betrayal’ after calling Putin ‘friend’
articles.summary: Hunter Biden, the son of former President Biden, went after President Trump over referring to Russian President Vladimir Putin as a “friend.” “The Great Betrayal. Of the allies who trusted us. Of the soldiers who served. Of every American who believed the office was larger than the man,” Hunter Biden said in a post Thursday…
articles.body:
Hunter Biden, the son of former President Biden, went after President Trump over referring to Russian President Vladimir Putin as a “friend.”

“The Great Betrayal. Of the allies who trusted us. Of the soldiers who served. Of every American who believed the office was larger than the man,” Hunter Biden said in a post Thursday afternoon on social platform X.

“He [Trump] stands for nothing but himself. History will hold both of these men accountable for their crimes,” he added.

Hunter Biden’s post featured a screenshot of a headline from the BBC about Trump’s comments.

The president greeted Putin as a “friend” Thursday , as the two arrived for a meeting in China.

“Who is he? He’s my friend,” Trump is heard saying, after walking into a room with his Russian counterpart.

Trump has a notably friendly relationship with Putin in spite of tension between Washington and Moscow in the last decade. The president was set to speak separately with Putin during a visit to Shenzhen , China, aside from a trilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping.

Putin and Trump’s meeting marks their first one-on-one since an August 2025 summit in Alaska, which was meant to further negotiations on the Russia-Ukraine war.

Trump told reporters earlier this week that he thought the Russian president was “backing down a bit” in the war in Ukraine, which will hit the five-year mark in February.

“I think he could be a lot tougher, frankly,” the president said. “I think he’s backing down. I think he’d like to, frankly, I think he’d like to see it finished.”

The Hill has reached out to the White House for comment.

articles.title: Heavy fighting erupts in Haiti as armed forces fight gangs to regain control of key corridor
articles.summary: SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico — Armed forces in Haiti launched an aggressive operation on Thursday to remove powerful gangs long entrenched in a key corridor that connects the country’s capital to its western and southern regions.
articles.body: SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico — Armed forces in Haiti launched an aggressive operation on Thursday to remove powerful gangs long entrenched in a key corridor that connects the country’s capital to its western and southern regions. It is the first significant operation in the five years since violent gangs seized control of Martissant, located in the western tip of Port-au-Prince. Haiti’s National Police posted a video on X stating that at least 34 suspected gang members were killed in Martissant during a fight with police officers working with a task force composed of members from Vectus Global, a private security firm founded by former U.S. Navy SEAL and Blackwater founder Erik Prince. Local media reported heavy gunfire and explosive drones in the area as Haiti’s police posted a video of armored vehicles rumbling through the community. Martissant is located along Route 2, the main road that leads out of Port-au-Prince to important western and southern cities. Thousands of people would travel through Martissant every day before gangs seized control of the area more than five years ago, disrupting the country’s economy as they prevented goods from entering or leaving the capital. Gangs have since charged tolls or randomly opened fire on cars or buses that dare cross through. Ever since gangs seized absolute control of Martissant, aid workers and Haitian civilians have been forced to take alternative transportation or use rural back roads. Forces wrestle with powerful gangs The fight to control Martissant began in June 2021, when gangs from Grand-Ravine and Village-de-Dieu attacked the Ti-Bois gang. Armed men set fire to homes, killed families, destroyed businesses and seized control of Martissant’s police station. The clashes forced at least 19,000 people to flee their homes and affected some 800,000 people overall, according to a July 2022 United Nations report. Several years ago, gangs operating between Tabarre and Carrefour would demand some $380 from those transiting through Martissant, according to a 2023 U.N. report. Last year, Haiti’s Center for Analysis and Research in Human Rights noted that ever since Martissant fell, hundreds of public and private institutions were relocated and more than one million people were forced to flee their homes. As the fight in Martissant continues, a U.N.-backed gang suppression force also has made recent inroads against gangs in a push to not only displace them but prevent their return. “Operations are entering a new phase: increasing pressure on gang networks, dismantling more strongholds, and extending control over strategic areas,” the force wrote Thursday on X. The gang suppression force said it’s working in places including Tabarre in Port-au-Prince and in Haiti’s central Artibonite region, which has come under repeated violent attacks by armed men. The force said it has come under fire as it advances along Route 5, “removing obstacles established by gangs to isolate communities and control key routes.” The force said it also cleared and secured a church and school that gangs had been controlling north of Gros-Morne. “It is about restoring freedom of movement, reopening access to public institutions, and re-establishing State presence for communities that have endured years of gang control,” the force wrote Sunday on X. El Salvador embraces gang fight Also fighting gangs are some 2,500 troops deployed by El Salvador last month when four of their own went missing after an Oct. 18 attack in Haiti’s capital. Following orders by Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele, the troops have attacked the main homes of two of Haiti’s most powerful gang leaders, Jeff and Lanmò San Jou, this month. Neither one was killed. Thousands of Haitians poured into the streets of Port-au-Prince and beyond this week in support of Bukele, but experts have criticized the unilateral operations of Salvadoran troops and noted that the use of explosive drones has claimed a growing number of innocent victims. A small group of Salvadorans are separately working with the gang suppression force. In late September, El Salvador’s legislature passed a law authorizing the participation of that group in Haiti for another 12 months until October 2027. The law was championed by Bukele and overwhelmingly approved by the country’s congress, controlled by Bukele’s party. The ongoing clashes with gangs continue as Haiti prepares for its first elections in more than a decade. The country hasn’t had a president since Jovenel Moïse was killed in July 2021.

articles.title: Rob Brydon says he invented his own fake agent to negotiate fees
articles.summary: The comedian and actor says he "invented a guy called Richard Knight" to negotiate on his behalf.
articles.body:
Rob Brydon has revealed he pretended to be his own agent at the start of his career when he was working as a TV and radio presenter in Wales.

The actor, best known for playing Stacey's Uncle Bryn in the hit sitcom Gavin and Stacey, told BBC One's Graham Norton Show he used to step into the role of his fake agent to arrange bookings for events.

"I would get asked to go and do things, and I didn't really have an agent at that time so I invented a guy called Richard Knight," Brydon told the show.

The fictional agent would phone organisers and negotiate a fee for Brydon's appearance, he said.

The actor, who grew up in Baglan, Port Talbot, shared an anecdote about being invited to a fundraiser and managing to get a fee for it.

"I'm terribly embarrassed," he told the show's host and fellow guests Cynthia Erivo, David Tennant and Laura Linney.

"They were all there for the good of their hearts," he said.

Brydon, known for his ability to mimic a range of celebrities, went on to impersonate the fictional Richard Knight asking for money in return for an appearance, with the agent describing Brydon as "an angel".

"I would go to these events and they would say 'oh I spoke to Mr Knight, he's quite a character', and I would say 'more than you realise'," Brydon told the show.

The 61-year-old actor stars in new sitcom Bill's Included in which he plays Bill Beam, a divorced man who rents his spare rooms to four students to stay financially afloat while "trying his very best to be their friend".

He told the Press Association he was drawn to his latest comedy role because he had missed acting in sitcoms since featuring in Gavin and Stacey.

The popular show ended in January 2010, although Christmas specials aired in 2019 and 2024.

While Brydon has since hosted shows including Destination X and Would I Lie To You?, the new show marks his return to the sitcom format.

"He calls himself a land-friend, not a landlord," Brydon said of his character Bill Beam.

Dylan Brady, Ada Player, Harry Baxendale and Yasmin Al-Khudhairi join the cast as Bill's student lodgers Christian, Hettie, James and Zahra.

Brydon praised the young actors, saying he "loved being around them, partly because of their energy".

He said he also enjoyed hearing their perspective on the industry.

"They knew who was being cast in what, who was directing which projects and it reminded me of how I used to be," he said.

The actor also remarked on the "odd" feeling of being told by some of the actors that they grew up watching him on television.

He said: "I remember that at the end of filming, one of them said to me, 'Thanks for being nice and for spending time with us between set-ups'.

"My reaction was, 'Well, of course I did. We're all actors on this show.'"

Bill's Included will be available on BBC iPlayer and BBC One from 20 November.

articles.title: Are Black Friday and Cyber Monday deals still worth it? I’ve covered sales for 6+ years — here’s my take
articles.summary: Are Black Friday and Cyber Monday deals actually worth it? Shopping experts share tips on what to buy, what to skip and how to find genuine discounts.
articles.body: Retailers started rolling out their early Black Friday and Cyber Monday deals this week, so I’m sure you’ve asked yourself: are these discounts actually worth it? I’ve covered the massive sales for over six years, and I can say with certainty that they offer some of the year’s lowest prices across categories. But it takes a little bit of work to find the absolute best deals, and you have to strategize beforehand to save the most money. To help you make a Black Friday and Cyber Monday game plan, I put together this guide filled with tips and tricks I swear by. I also talked to experts to get their advice about what to buy, what to skip, how to find the top deals and whether shopping in-person versus online makes a difference anymore. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. What are the best things to buy during Black Friday and Cyber Monday? Tech If you have electronics on your wish list — or are buying a gift for someone who does — now is your time to buy. Tech sees some of the strongest discounts during Black Friday and Cyber Monday, especially when it comes to devices like TVs, headphones and video game consoles, says Ashley Feinstein Gerstley, a shopping and savings strategist at Rakuten, an online and in-store cashback platform. As a baseline, Vipin Porwal, the founder and consumer savings expert at Smarty, an online shopping rewards app, expects at least 30 percent off in most cases, except for TVs and computers, which are usually in the 20 to 25 percent off range. Black Friday and Cyber Monday video game bundles are particularly lucrative. It’s one of the only times a year I see brands like Nintendo, Xbox and PlayStation sell their most popular console, game and digital subscription for less than each item would cost if you bought them individually. Related deals 55% off NBA 2K27 on PS545% off the Nothing Headphone (a) 202628% off the Apple AirPods Pro 3 Toys Toys is one of the most competitive categories during Black Friday and Cyber Monday, both in terms of discounts and demand. You usually get at least 30 percent off, says Porwal, and the most popular toys sell out quickly — I’m talking a couple of hours, maximum. Once you see prices drop, buy your must-haves immediately. Some of the hottest toys and collectibles to watch this season are the Beyblade X, Jellycats, KPop Demon Hunters toys, Lego Pokémon and SMART Play, NeeDohs, Pokémon Pikachu Puppetronic, Sesame Street Tickle Me Elmo Giggle Max and Toy Story 5 toys, according to Adobe. Related deals 40% off the LeapFrog My Best Pal Scout30% off the Lego Creator 3-in-1 Forest Animals: Red Fox25% off the Yoto Mini 2024 Edition Clothes and shoes Clothes and shoes typically get marked down by at least 20 to 25 percent during Black Friday and Cyber Monday, says Porwal. Many brands run sitewide sales, so their entire inventory is marked down, while department stores and big-box retailers put most of their stock on clearance to get rid of it before the new year. Related deals 42% off the Hoka Arahi 841% off the Gap 100% Cotton Softest Flannel PJ Set33% off the Beyond Yoga Spacedye Dynamic Performance Cropped Tank Small home and kitchen appliances Almost every small home and kitchen appliance you can think of gets discounted during Black Friday and Cyber Monday, including that Vitamix blender or Dyson vacuum you’re dreaming about. In addition to items you use year-round, keep an eye on seasonal appliances, like space heaters and snow blowers, as well as tableware, home decor and other essentials you’ll need to host guests during the holidays, says Gerstley. Related deals 44% off the Roborock Q7 M5+ Robot Vacuum and Mop44% off the Shark Vertex Lift-Away Upright Vacuum35% off the De’Longhi Classic Signature Espresso Machine Subscriptions, experiences and activities Don’t forget to think beyond tangible products during Black Friday and Cyber Monday, says Mackenzie Shand, executive editor at RetailMeNot, a digital coupon, promo code and cashback platform. There are lots of deals on subscriptions, experiences and activities, too. “Many streaming services host Black Friday and Cyber Monday sales, which can lower the cost of your entertainment bill for the entire year,” she says. “Meanwhile, if you have travel plans coming up, be on the lookout for deals on things like passes to zoos, aquariums and other recreation-type places in your area.” Fitness classes, gym memberships, beauty appointments, educational platforms and event tickets also often drop in price. Additionally, while Travel Tuesday, on December 1 this year, is a dedicated day for travel deals, you’ll start seeing offers well before then. Hotels, resorts, tour groups, rental home and car booking companies, cruise lines and flight booking platforms are starting to roll out their sales now, making it the ideal time to plan a trip. You’ll see travel essentials on sale, too, like suitcases, toiletry bags and packing cubes. Related deals Get 50% off an annual subscription to The Sculpt SocietyGet 30% off or more on select Expedia vacation packages through Dec. 3Get any monthly Paramount+ plan for $2.99 per month for your first two months through Nov. 30 Gift cards and sets Because retailers know Black Friday and Cyber Monday are prime times for holiday shopping, many discount gift cards for literally everything: stores across categories, restaurants, movie theatres, spas, streaming services, food delivery platforms, and more. “As long as you plan to gift or use this gift card, you are basically getting free money from these deals,” says Shand. There are also strong discounts on gift sets, like those that bundle beauty products, gourmet food and beverages, travel essentials and accessories. You buy these sets, wrap them and give them to your recipient rather than having to curate a selection yourself. Related deals Get a $100 DoorDash gift card for $85Get a $50 $50 Aéropostale gift card for $40Get a Giftory AMC Movie Night Gift Card for 24% off What products should you avoid buying during Black Friday and Cyber Monday? No category is totally off limits during Black Friday and Cyber Monday — if you do the work, you can find a worthwhile deal on almost anything since the majority of retailers participate in the biggest shopping events of the year. But if you’re trying to narrow down your list, here’s what experts recommend waiting on and when to buy it instead: Winter clothes and shoes: wait until end-of-season clearance sales in January and FebruaryMattresses, furniture and major home and kitchen appliances: wait until three-day holiday weekend sales like Presidents’ DayBed and bath linens, like sheets and towels: wait until “white sales” in January and three-day holiday weekend sales like Presidents’ DayFitness equipment: wait until New Year’s sales in JanuaryHoliday decor: wait until after the holiday season to refresh your collection and save it for next year Are Black Friday and Cyber Monday deals worse than last year? No, Black Friday and Cyber Monday deals aren’t worse than last year, but they’re not dramatically better either, says Claudia Townsend, a consumer behavior researcher and expert and marketing professor at the University of Miami. “Prices have risen, while discount percentages are likely to remain roughly the same as last year,” she says. “This means that a 25 percent discount, for example, will yield a higher final price if the item’s starting price is higher than it was a year ago.” That said, Black Friday and Cyber Monday are still the biggest, highest-revenue days for retail of the year. Retailers want to draw customers in with deals, so most save their lowest prices for late November. But a discount isn’t a compelling enough reason alone for shoppers to spend anymore, says Shand — they’re being much more thoughtful about scoping out real deals to get the best overall value, not just the lowest price. How do you find the best Black Friday and Cyber Monday deals? 1. Make a shopping list and set a budget “The most common mistake is allowing in-the-moment sales and marketing cues define one’s shopping list,” says Townsend. “That’s how people end up “saving” 40 percent on items they never intended to buy. I recommend that consumers create a list with a budget and a target price for each item, and commit to purchasing only when a deal reaches that price.” Some retailers let you make shopping lists in their apps or on their websites and, along with certain cashback extensions, let you set up notifications when items’ prices drop so you can start evaluating immediately. That means you don’t have to do any browsing that might lead to impulse purchases — you stay zeroed in on your list the entire time. 2. Track prices Free tools like CamelCamelCamel, Keepa and Honey show you a product’s price history, as do built-in features on some retailers’ websites. Use them to determine whether an item dropped in price from a steady baseline, making it a legitimate deal, or if it’s marked down from an inflated baseline. Be sure to also use price-tracking tools to figure out what a specific product cost during Black Friday and Cyber Monday last year. That serves as a great comparison point, especially for early deals: If a product’s price dropped more during last year’s Black Friday to Cyber Monday period than the two weeks before it, you can expect a brand to follow the same pattern this year, giving you an idea about when you should finally add to cart and check out. Overall, “if the deal price matches or beats the item’s lowest price over the past year, it’s likely a good deal,” says Townsend. 3. Compare prices across retailers Before checking out, compare the price of a specific product across multiple retailers to make sure you’re getting the absolute lowest offer, says Shand. Look beyond the actual discount, too. Factor in shipping fees, extra perks like free installation and where you get the most cash back, for example. 4. Stack your savings The discount itself is your starting point. Can you bring down the price even more by signing up for email or SMS lists and getting an extra promo code; using a cashback extension; becoming a free loyalty member and earning rewards as you shop; or paying with a credit card that lets you earn points or cash back? 5. Research price matching policies If there’s a product at the top of your or your loved one’s wish list, get it as soon as it goes on sale, so long as the retailer you’re shopping at has a price-matching policy. “If a retailer will refund the difference should the price drop more, there’s little downside to buying,” says Townsend. 6. Start shopping early Retailers stretch Black Friday and Cyber Monday out across the entire month of November, so there’s no reason to wait to buy a product if you do everything you can to make sure it’s a good deal now. In fact, because so many customers are vying for the same products, and retailers limit quantities of certain products, shopping early might be the only way to get an item in the exact color, size and style you want. “Sometimes, finding the product you actually want in stock is the deal,” says Shand. “A great deal doesn’t do you much good if the product is gone.” Meet our shopping experts Claudia Townsend is a consumer behavior researcher and expert and marketing professor at the University of Miami.Ashley Feinstein Gerstley is a shopping and savings strategist at Rakuten, an online and in-store cashback platform.Mackenzie Shand is the executive editor at RetailMeNot, a digital coupon, promo code and cashback platform.Vipin Porwal is the founder and consumer savings expert at Smarty, an online shopping rewards app. Why trust NBC Selected? I’m a reporter at NBC Selected who has covered deals and sales for over six years. I write about the best overall discounts during Black Friday and Cyber Monday, as well as chart the history of both sales and what to buy versus skip. I regularly appear in related NBC News NOW and TODAY Show segments, too. To write this article, I interviewed four experts about Black Friday and Cyber Monday. Catch up on NBC Selected’s in-depth coverage of tech and tools, wellness and more, and follow us on Facebook, Instagram, X and TikTok to stay up to date.
