articles.title: Democrat lawmaker hit with federal indictment over alleged $240K COVID fraud scheme
articles.summary: Alabama Rep. Patrick Sellers allegedly obtained more than $240,000 through fraudulent applications and used the money for personal expenses.
articles.body: An Alabama state representative has been indicted for allegedly orchestrating an extensive fraud scheme to obtain private and taxpayer-backed loans and grants to fund his personal expenses, the Justice Department announced Thursday. Officials identified the lawmaker as Patrick Lorn Sellers, 53, who has represented a district near Birmingham since November 2022 and was recently re-elected to a second term. Sellers was also a church pastor and former chief of staff to the president of the Alabama State Missionary Baptist Convention (ASMBC). Between July 2020 and May 2021, Sellers allegedly siphoned more than $240,000 in grants and loans intended to provide relief during the COVID-19 pandemic, according to the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Alabama. MINNESOTA FRAUD MASTERMIND GETS NEARLY 42 YEARS IN PRISON IN MASSIVE $250M 'FEEDING OUR FUTURE' SCHEME The alleged scheme specifically targeted the federal and state governments and a private nonprofit. Those benefits were used to cover personal expenses, including credit card bills, mortgage payments, auto loan payments, water bills and even his daughters' college tuition, officials said. In one notable instance, Sellers allegedly took control of an affiliate nonprofit belonging to ASMBC and applied for pandemic relief funds without notifying the convention’s president or board. After Sellers obtained the money, the charity's actual leaders were denied funding when they legitimately attempted to apply for assistance, officials said. DOJ’S ‘OPERATION GHOSTBUSTERS’ TARGETS MASSIVE STUDENT-AID FRAUD SCHEME BUILT ON FAKE ENROLLEES He also repeatedly lied on federal and state relief applications, claiming he operated multiple nonprofits that employed as many as 10 people when, in reality, he had no employees, according to prosecutors. In addition, Sellers reportedly claimed to operate a landscaping business and fabricated tax forms for returns he had never filed with the IRS. GOP LAWMAKER’S FRAUD CRUSADE TAKES DRAMATIC TURN AS SCANDAL ENGULFS HIS OWN CAREER "Under U.S. Attorney Williams, we have a mandate to aggressively pursue corrupt public officials, no matter what position they hold or what power they wield," Assistant U.S. Attorney Brett A. Janich said in a statement. Because the payouts were handled electronically across state lines, Sellers now faces four felony counts of wire fraud alongside strict demands to forfeit the illegally obtained funds. The maximum penalty for wire fraud is up to 20 years in prison. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The FBI investigated the matter, and assistant U.S. attorneys Brett A. Janich and Ryan S. Rummage are prosecuting the case.

articles.title: Masked protesters chant 'Charlie Kirk deserved to die' outside TPUSA event at University of Washington
articles.summary: Videos show masked protesters chanting outside Chloe Cole's TPUSA event at the University of Washington, including some cheering Charlie Kirk's assassination.
articles.body: Masked activists protesting a Turning Point USA (TPUSA) event at the University of Washington Wednesday celebrated TPUSA founder Charlie Kirk’s assassination. Since Kirk's murder in September 2025, Turning Point USA has hosted a series of Pick Up the Mic campus events where influencers spark conversations with students to continue Kirk's legacy. Chloe Cole, a detransitioner who advocates against youth gender transition, was slated to speak at the event. Cole canceled a scheduled speech at the university in May because of alleged violent threats from Antifa. On Wednesday night, protesters gathered on the lawn outside the event, waving the transgender pride flag and holding signs with messages opposing Cole and Kirk. INSIDE CHARLIE KIRK’S EFFORT TO DEVELOP THE NEXT GENERATION OF CONSERVATIVE VOICES Videos circulating online showed protesters who identified themselves as members of the American Party of Labor Puget Sound chanting, "Charlie Kirk deserved to die," and carrying signs that said "Women hold up half the sky, Charlie Kirk deserved to die" and "Kirk's pronouns were was/were." The group reposted several of the videos to its social media accounts acknowledging the chanting with one post saying, "Guilty!!" When asked about the protest, a spokesperson for the University of Washington told Fox News Digital, "The safety and security of our entire community, including event participants, observers and passersby, is our top priority. The scheduled event occurred without disruption, and protesters outside exercised their right to free expression." UNIVERSITY PRESIDENT SOUNDS ALARM AS NEARLY HALF OF STUDENTS JUSTIFY VIOLENCE TO STOP 'HATE SPEECH' Theo Wold, a former White House deputy assistant for domestic policy during President Donald Trump's first term, commented on the incident in a statement to Fox News Digital. "The left is defined by mass movement politics with roots in the violence and barbarism of the French Revolution and the Red Terror of the Spanish Civil War," he said. "Elite institutions paper over the growing threat of Antifa Democrats, anarchist direct action and revolutionary violence because they don’t want Americans to understand leftist radicalism for what it is. "But this pattern of incidents cannot be shrugged away as ‘mere’ intimidation. It is another example of this radical movement and its easy acceptance of violence." articles.title: Feds release brazen heist video, charge 14 in alleged $22.5M California freight train theft ring
articles.summary: Fourteen suspects face federal charges in an alleged $22.5 million cargo theft scheme targeting 36 freight trains in Southern California.
articles.body: At least 14 suspects have been federally charged with orchestrating a $22.5 million cargo theft scheme that targeted at least 36 freight trains in Southern California, the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Central District of California announced Thursday. The crew's leader was identified as Nathan Daniel Angel, 21, of East Los Angeles, who allegedly ran the operation alongside his father and two uncles. Officials also released video of the brazen heist that appeared to have been filmed by some of the crew members. In the clip, members are seen sawing through cargo doors, grabbing boxes and flashing peace signs as they ransacked the trains. "The scale of the theft is staggering," First Assistant United States Attorney Bill Essayli said. "We will prosecute the people who raid these trains and those who knowingly turn stolen cargo into cash." CARGO THEFT HITS EVERYTHING FROM LEGO TO TEQUILA. WE NEED THE SENATE TO HELP STOP IT HUNDREDS OF THOUSANDS OF DOLLARS IN STOLEN GOODS RECOVERED AT A USED CAR LOT AFTER ADULT TOY COMPANY PURCHASE From February 2024 to August 2026, Nathan Angel allegedly led a group of co-conspirators in targeting freight trains carrying high-value goods for resale on the black market. The trains reportedly carried Nike sneakers, Milwaukee tools, electronics and other products that entered the U.S. through the Ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach from international destinations. According to prosecutors, Nathan Angel and his co-conspirators allegedly planned their thefts in advance by selecting specific locations along railroad tracks where they could force trains to stop. Once the trains reached these preselected locations, members of the group cut the air hoses to trigger an emergency stop, officials alleged. As the trains came to a halt, other crew members allegedly used trucks or vans to drive to the designated locations and board the trains, while additional members acted as lookouts. The alleged thieves then transported the goods to stash houses, including properties belonging to some of the suspects. The crew then coordinated their thefts through Instagram while discussing resale prices for the stolen products, prosecutors alleged. NEARLY $1M IN GRADED TRADING CARDS STOLEN FROM FEDEX TRUCK OUTSIDE PSA FACILITY IN SANTA ANA Officials said one buyer was a representative of a Los Angeles-based business known as a sneaker and streetwear resale brand. The business was not an authorized Nike reseller, officials said. That business alone reportedly generated more than $1 million for the crew by purchasing thousands of pairs of stolen Nike sneakers between May 2025 and October 2025. The crew leader's family members named in the case include his father, Daniel Angel, 38, of East Los Angeles, and his uncles, Rodolfo Angel, 23, and Jose Luis Angel, 23, both of East Los Angeles. The other defendants include Donta Hedgeman, 27, Fernando Alexis Alvarado Villegas, 27, Daniel Garcia, 36, Carlos Robert Estrada, 28, Angel Sanchez, 24, Ruben Mario Banuelos, 26, Fredy Marquina, 25, Carlos Luis Fernando Martinez, 23, Jorge Angel Aguilar Espinoza, 36, and Ricardo Mares, 32. "Train robberies cause enormous economic damage because of the valuable cargo involved. These defendants face long federal prison sentences if convicted. All are presumed innocent until proven guilty," Essayli said. The arrests followed a 14-month investigation that involved the Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), the Los Angeles Police Department Commercial Crimes Bureau, the Union Pacific Railroad Police Department, the California Highway Patrol Cargo Theft Interdiction Program and the IRS Criminal Investigation. Additionally, each count of violence against railroad cars carries a maximum penalty of life in prison.
